## TL;DR

Addressed review round 1’s rendered coverage finding by adding Releases and Deployments as dedicated screen states in the audit. Built the app and reran `bun run contrast:audit` with headless WebKit. It passed across 16 theme scopes and 16 screen states, examining 16,502 visible text runs with no text below the WCAG floor. Updated the QA record to match the expanded coverage and current results.

## Work and rationale

The review pointed out that the rendered contrast audit had no Releases or deployment screen state. That was a real omission: the repository’s existing November theme QA note explicitly distinguished layout coverage from rendered contrast coverage and said Releases/deployment were excluded. I inspected the audit’s screen preparation list, fixture setup, and router routes. The fixture already supplies a running app with API fallbacks and the route table exposes `/releases` and `/deployments`, so direct route preparations are the narrowest useful way to make those screens part of every theme pass.

I added two named screen states to `makeScreens`: `releases` visits `/releases`, and `deployments` visits `/deployments`. They use the same `gotoApp` preparation as other page states. This causes the existing rendered probe to run on their visible text and computed backgrounds for each configured theme scope, while keeping contrast thresholds, exemptions, fixture data, and theme configuration unchanged.

I built with `bun run build` because the ignored `dist/` artifacts are needed by the audit command. The build succeeded. I then ran `bun run contrast:audit`; the output confirmed 16 theme scopes × 16 screen states and reported 16,502 visible text runs examined. It found no text below the WCAG floor. The run separately counted 320 exemptions, 70 disabled-component runs, zero invisible runs, 8,724 gradient worst-stop judgments, and 18 unchecked `background-clip: text` runs for the gradient logo. These are classifications reported by the probe, not new failures or exemptions.

I revised `docs/qa/2026-11-theme-contrast-qa.md` to describe the expanded route coverage and replace all stale screen/run counts. The document retains the audit limitation for gradient-clipped logo text and the existing collapsed-column exemption rationale. No theme color changes were justified by the run, and no exemption was added.

## Approaches tried

I first cross-checked the automated review against `docs/qa/2026-11-themes.md` and the actual `makeScreens` implementation. That confirmed the reviewer was right: the earlier QA report’s broad wording implied all main surfaces had rendered coverage even though Releases/Deployments were absent. I considered the existing separate Playwright layout pass, but it was not adequate for this issue because it checks widths and page stability rather than text contrast. I therefore extended the rendered audit itself.

The two route states deliberately use simple navigation and the existing shared probe. This avoids a second custom contrast mechanism and means both pages are tested in all configured dark and light theme variants, alongside the existing drawers and other states. I did not modify `repoos.toml`, theme token definitions, or audit exemptions.

## Challenges and blockers

The main implementation detail was choosing where to attach coverage. The audit uses one shared fixture server and visits each screen before iterating every scope. Adding states to this matrix directly exercises both pages without separate app startup or a duplicate test path. The fixture does not model live production release/deployment infrastructure; the rendered pages still load through their fixture-backed API behavior, so the audit measures the UI states that the fixture can present. It does not claim to verify remote provider connectivity or a real deploy.

The audit marks `background-clip: text` logo runs as unchecked. I kept that limitation visible in the QA record instead of describing the run as measuring every rendered pixel. The audit also retains the previously documented collapsed board column exemption; this pass did not change its policy.

## Key learnings

A layout QA pass over Releases does not satisfy a rendered text-contrast audit. When an audit report claims broad page coverage, its prepared route list must include the actual pages named by the QA scope. The existing rendered harness can cover additional pages with named route states and apply the same scope-and-probe loop consistently. After this extension, the audit itself confirms 16 states under all 16 configured theme scopes, and the resulting QA record now reports that evidence precisely.
